title: Beignets koki (Cowpea Fritters)
author: Tata Ngome et al. (CIFOR-ICRAF, IRAD, Université de Ngaoundéré)
desc: Cowpeas soaked 6 hours, skinned, crushed with chilli and onion into a light, fine paste, salted and spooned into hot oil.
longDesc: A page from the October 2023 northern-Cameroon recipe book. The cowpeas are covered with water and soaked 6 hours, pressed between the hands to remove the thin skin and rinsed. They are crushed finely with the chilli and onion with a little water and stirred until the paste is light and fine; salt is added. Balls are formed with a ladle or spoon and fried in hot oil. The page prints no frying time, oil temperature or colour cue.
ingredients: Oil for frying — quantity not printed
steps: Cover the cowpeas with water and soak for 6 hours.
Press the beans between your hands to remove the thin skin, then rinse.
Crush finely with the chilli and onion, adding a little water.
Stir the paste until light and fine. Add the salt.
Shape balls with a ladle or spoon and fry in hot oil.
chefTips: The printed texture cue is a paste that is ‘légère et fine’ (light and fine).
Rubbing the soaked beans together is how the skin comes off.
The page prints no frying time or temperature; fry to colour and check one fritter for doneness.
commonMistakes: Making the paste too wet so the balls fall apart in the oil.
Oil that is not hot enough.
healthBenefits: Cowpeas are plant protein and fibre; frying adds oil.
culturalNote: The book names no community for its recipes; the attribution is ‘the northern part of Cameroon’.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Beignets koki (niébé)’ (p. 56). Authors as printed: ‘Tata Ngome et al.’; October 2023 (V1), © 2024, CC BY 4.0. Soak ‘6 heures’. Yield not printed (servings 4 is a placeholder; prep 20 is a placeholder). TWO-PASS.
ABSENT: frying time, oil temperature, finished colour, oil quantity.
